newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia wool sector lobbies for tariff cuts.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia wool sector lobbies for tariff cuts.

text.p: The Australian wool industry is pressing for the dismantling of Australian tariffs on textiles and clothing as part of a drive for international tariff cuts.
Rod Thirkell-Johnston, president of woolgrower organisation Wool Council of Australia (WCA), said on Monday he had met Australian Minister for Trade Tim Fischer on the issue.
Fischer had demonstrated a strong commitment to trade liberalisation and awareness of the enormous benefit to woolgrowers of tariff and quota reductions, he said.
The WCA highlighted quotas and tariffs in the U.S., China and India in a statement.
"These countries will be the focus of our efforts in the next 12 months. These three markets currently consume about one-third of Australia's total wool production," Thirkell-Johnston said.
Australian woolgrowers would benefit by A$157 million in the first year from abolition of tariffs and quotas in the U.S. alone, he said.
Apparel prices would fall by 17 percent and demand increase by almost 15 percent in the U.S. domestic market, he said.
Australia imposes import tariffs of five percent on worsted yarn, 23 percent on worsted fabric and 37 percent on men's and women's clothing.
China imposes tariffs of 15 percent on wool imports, 20 percent on worsted yarn, 35 percent on worsted fabric and mostly 45 percent on imported clothing.
India imposes a 27 percent tariff on imported greasy wool, 52 percent on wool tops and 52 percent on imported worsted yarn, fabric and clothing.

The U.S. imposes a 20.9 cents a kg tariff on greasy wool, 5.6 percent plus 6.9 cents a kg on wool tops, 33.9 percent on worsted fabric, 20.6 percent plus 47.6 cents a kg on men's suits and other tariffs across the imported clothing range.
